findings.title: Opening connective into command
findings.claim: The opening wa links the closing utterance to an ongoing address and immediately leads into qul, so praise arrives as speech to be performed.
findings.mechanism: The conjunction is attached to the second-person imperative that governs the following praise formula; their contact makes the verse a connected command rather than a detached summary.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears the closing as an act the addressee must voice, not only a proposition to observe.
findings.containment: The local connective and imperative support this reading; the specific preceding instruction and its relation at 17:110 are not established in this micro packet.

epistemic.reason: The local wa-to-qul relation is supplied and trusted; the cited predecessor is excluded because no context unit is projected.

findings.title: Praise as performed speech
findings.claim: The imperative qul makes the praise formula an utterance assigned to the addressee, turning the verse's theology into speech to perform.
findings.mechanism: A direct second-person command governs al-hamdu lillah as its spoken content; the grammatical relation makes the praise an act of saying rather than an unaddressed statement.
findings.reader_payoff: The addressee is given words to say, so the verse is heard as enacted praise.
findings.containment: This is the local force of the imperative and its complement; the separate predecessor claim at 17:110 is not carried.

epistemic.reason: The imperative, its person, and its governed praise content are directly supplied in QAC and trusted word analysis.

findings.title: Praise as a standing category
findings.claim: Al-hamdu names praise as a definite category, and the denials that follow let it read as praise for what God is rather than only thanks for a benefit.
findings.mechanism: The praise noun is assigned to God before the relative clause describes him as free of offspring, co-rule, and need; those independent descriptions activate the praise-versus-thanks distinction while leaving thanks available elsewhere.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the opening gives God praise as a standing due, not merely gratitude for a particular gift.
findings.containment: The extension to thanksgiving remains part of the branch's range, but this local passage supplies no particular benefit as its trigger; the cited echo to 1:2 is not used.

epistemic.reason: The definite nominative praise category, its attribution, and the following descriptions are all supplied in the focus packet.

epistemic.reason: The partner noun, domain phrase, and exact focus branch are supplied; the move from co-holder to a divine-prerogative attribution is an interpretive contact.

findings.title: The named act intensifies the command
findings.claim: Takbiran is the cognate accusative of kabbirhu, naming and intensifying the very act the command asks the addressee to perform.
findings.mechanism: The verbal noun repeats the preceding Form II root as an accusative of manner or emphasis, not as a second object, and occupies the final word position.
findings.reader_payoff: The ayah ends by naming magnification itself, so its last word completes rather than merely follows the command.
findings.containment: The cognate-accusative relation is local; the cross-ayah frame at 17:1 is not used, and the word does not mean a second object.

epistemic.reason: The supplied attachment analysis identifies the verbal noun and its intensifying relation.

findings.title: The denials become spoken praise
findings.claim: What first reads as divine attributes with praise appended can also be heard as a commanded voiced verdict: the denials supply praise's grounds, and the doubled closing root performs magnification.
findings.mechanism: Qul carries speech outward, al-hamd supplies its evaluative center, and kabbirhu with takbiran turns recognition of greatness into the commanded close.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears the whole ayah as a proclamation to enact, not a silent inventory followed by an extra phrase.
findings.containment: This remains a local, attributed synthesis of the supplied focus words; it does not claim a wider channel or that the command increases God in reality.

epistemic.reason: The three HFT roles are legacy_unbound, but their roots, branch records, and word coordinates match supplied focus occurrences; the synthesis remains attributed.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Çekirdek işlem, sözü sesli olarak dışa çıkarmaktır.
branch_activations.carrier: Qul is the imperative that voices words.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The separate al-hamd formula supplies the utterance's content and the closing kabbirhu-takbiran supplies a second commanded speech act.
branch_activations.activation: The opening spoken-word carrier meets praise content and a closing verbal command, turning the whole sequence into performance.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The ayah is a spoken proclamation rather than only a silent list of attributes.
branch_activations.boundary: This is a local reading of the focus sequence and not a claim about a recurring surah-wide channel.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: yermenin karşıtı olan, iyilik için teşekkürü de kapsayan övgü
branch_activations.facet_statement: İyi sözlerle övme, yermenin karşıtıdır.
branch_activations.carrier: Al-hamd carries praise as evaluation.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The command to speak and the distinct denials supply a voiced occasion and the content being evaluated.
branch_activations.activation: The praise branch meets an explicit instruction to say it and a sequence of descriptions, placing praise at the evaluative center of the proclamation.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The three negated dependencies are voiced as the grounds for praise rather than left as a silent attribute list.
branch_activations.boundary: The HFT role is retained as attributed; it does not decide that praise is the only effect of the ayah.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Ululuk, üstünlük ve başkalarından yukarıda olma düşüncesi anlamın temel eksenidir.
branch_activations.carrier: Kabbirhu and takbiran carry the greatness and magnification root in command and verbal-noun forms.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The named divine object and the preceding dependency denials establish the one whose greatness is declared.
branch_activations.activation: The greatness carrier meets the stated divine referent and the closing act of speech, while the human self-superiority facet is not needed.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The close voices God's greatness as the culmination of the praise proclamation.
branch_activations.boundary: Only the core greatness facet is active; human arrogance and any ontological increase are not claimed.

findings.title: Three routes of dependence closed
findings.claim: The clauses can be read as closing three supports of human rule: taking offspring for oneself, sharing sovereign administration, and receiving protection from weakness.
findings.mechanism: Yattakhidh meets walad as acquisition meets lineage; sharik meets mulk as participation meets the field of sovereignty; wali meets dhull through min as patronage meets the vulnerability that would call for it. The repeated negators keep the three contacts cumulative.
findings.reader_payoff: Instead of three disconnected denials, the reader sees a local account of dominion that needs neither dynastic continuation, co-administration, nor rescue from weakness.
findings.containment: The plain denials remain fully recoverable. The dependency synthesis is qualified HFT evidence at this ayah and does not establish a broader theological system or external recurrence.

epistemic.reason: All six HFT coordinates match the supplied focus roots and QAC occurrences, but the roles and synthesis originate in a legacy_unbound reconstructed trace.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şeyi kendisi için edinip kendine ait hale getirmeyi anlatır.
branch_activations.carrier: Yattakhidh carries taking or acquisition for oneself.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The following walad is a separate object naming offspring.
branch_activations.activation: Self-acquisition meets the offspring object, making the denied relation an acquired support or possession as well as a child relation.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The first denial closes a route to dynastic continuation through a child taken for oneself.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not add a particular adoption custom or treat the object as a literal possession.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: ana babadan doğan kişi veya kişiler
branch_activations.facet_statement: Temel gönderim, bir ana babadan doğmuş kişidir.
branch_activations.carrier: Walad carries the born-person or offspring relation.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Yattakhidh and lam separately place that relation under denied self-directed taking.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The first denial removes dynastic continuation from the dependency pattern.
branch_activations.boundary: The trace does not change the noun into a birth verb or specify a family practice.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şey, hak veya iş en az iki taraf arasında ortaktır ve taraflardan yalnız birine ait değildir.
branch_activations.carrier: Sharik names participation in a shared right or work.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Mulk separately names the field in which that participation would occur.
branch_activations.activation: The sharing branch meets a sovereign domain, making the denied partnership a possible co-administration of rule.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: No divided administration occupies the divine dominion.
branch_activations.boundary: The trace concerns partnership in mulk and does not generalize to every human partnership.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Hükümdar, halk üzerinde emir ve yasak koyarak kamusal yönetim yetkisi kullanır.
branch_activations.carrier: Al-mulk carries public rule and sovereignty.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The denied sharik and the separately named Allah specify the field and holder of that rule.
branch_activations.activation: Public sovereignty meets the explicit denial of a partner, so the field is read as undivided administration.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The sovereign domain has no co-administrator.
branch_activations.boundary: This core facet describes the rule relation and does not by itself assert the specialization of all-being absolute sovereignty.

branch_activations.facet_statement: İlahi bağlamda bütün varlık üzerindeki mutlak ve kalıcı egemenlik anlatılır.
branch_activations.carrier: Al-mulk carries the sovereignty branch.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The word Allah supplies the divine setting, while the partner denial specifies what cannot share that domain.
branch_activations.activation: The core rule sense meets the named divine referent and no-partner phrase, activating the branch's divine specialization while retaining its core facet above.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The dominion is heard as God's enduring sovereignty over all being, not only as a human administrative office.
branch_activations.boundary: This is a local specialization supplied by the branch record and focus relation; it makes no claim about context beyond 17:111.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir işi veya başkasının durumunu üstlenip yönetme ve yürütme.
branch_activations.carrier: Waliyyun carries taking responsibility for another's affairs.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Min al-dhull separately names the condition from which an external protector or manager would arise.
branch_activations.activation: The responsibility sense meets the stated vulnerability source and the negated existential frame, linking protection with a need to manage weakness.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The third denial closes dependence on a guardian who would take charge because of abasement.
branch_activations.boundary: The trace does not claim that God manages another's weakness or activate unrelated wali senses.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: hor ve güçsüz duruma düşüp boyun eğme
branch_activations.facet_statement: Kişi, saygınlık ve karşı koyma gücü bakımından aşağı bir konuma düşer ve boyun eğer.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The verse denies protection arising from a vulnerability that would make such support necessary.
branch_activations.boundary: The source record varies on coercion as a requirement; the trace carries weakness and abasement without making force mandatory.
